macovedj opened PR #14518 from macovedj:p2-tcp-close-unread-rst to bytecodealliance:main:

Closing a P2 TCP socket with unread received data currently shuts down its retained streams before closing the native descriptor. The peer can therefore observe a clean EOF instead of the connection reset expected when closing a socket with unread data.

This PR resets connected sockets with unread data before their retained streams drop, using zero linger plus connect(AF_UNSPEC) on Linux/Android and disconnectx on Apple targets.

pchickey commented on PR #14518:

Like #14461 I would need @badeend to take a look at this

badeend commented on PR #14518:

Hi! Could you maybe elaborate a bit on what problem this solves? Is there an application that relies on the peer seeing a reset? At first sight, I wouldn't expect the RST guarantee to offer much value in practice: any guest that buffers reads in memory (which is e.g. Node.js’s default), would already have drained the kernel buffer, so closing it sends a FIN anyway.

A more practical concern is that WASI 0.3 has no explicit close for sockets. The OS socket closes automatically once the last resource derived from it is dropped. So if this turns out to be a real problem, P3 has it too, and P3 can’t be fixed under the current spec. Changing only P2 makes it behave in a way 0.3 can’t express. If we decide this RST is worth guaranteeing to guests, I think the 0.3 spec should be updated to support it first, so that 0.2 stays implementable on top of 0.3 and won't need special host magic.
